# Activation Clause

Maintains one party roster, records acceptance of identified terms, and guards document processing according to acceptance and access readiness. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. Executable hooks come from the admitted exact clause type. All paths below belong to the document where the clause executes.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied through `parameters`; runtime functions read `/clauses/activation/parameters`.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by valid party names. Each party needs `lead/channel`; keys in optional `representatives` must also pass name validation. The precise name and transport-validation rules are inherited and are not included here.
- `required` lists parties whose acceptance is needed and defaults to all initial roster keys. `revision` starts at the configured value, defaulting to `1`.
- `allowNewParties`, default `false`, permits direct additions through `updateParty_<role>`. Initial `frozen` is true if either the parameter is true or `/partyRosterFrozen` is true; otherwise its parameter default is false. Freezing prevents roster updates and approved admissions.
- `accessPaths`, default `[]`, identifies embedded access documents to process and monitor. `readers`, default `{}`, participates in access validation. `/partyAccess` is also processed as a collection of embedded access documents.
- `preActivationOperations`, `preActivationChannels` and `preActivationTimerChannels` each default to `[]` and configure dispatch exceptions described below.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths`, default `[]`, enables negotiation when nonempty. This requires at least one required approver and a document `type`. Each path must identify an existing scalar field: text, integer, double or Boolean. Paths must be distinct, begin with `/`, contain no empty segments or `~`, and cannot start under `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`. They cannot equal or descend from an `accessPaths` entry.
- `admission/approvers` must be nonempty for the separate approved-admission operation. The supplied implementation does not establish how those approvals are collected.

Ordinary clause transitions cannot replace this clause's configuration: roster changes use party operations. While negotiation is configured and the document has never activated, changes to the clause configuration set are rejected with `NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`. Conflicting channel or party contract names also cause rejection.

## State and access

`/activation` holds the roster in `parties`, required approver keys in `required`, and recorded party acceptances in `approved`. Its integer `revision` identifies the activation revision being reviewed; it is not a timestamp.

`accessReady` and `functional` contain the same computed access result. Access checks include the current roster and additions in `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current revision. `termsAccepted` requires every listed required party's approval plus the inherited `termsCurrent` check. A missing approval entry counts as unapproved in this calculation. `active` additionally requires access readiness and an unset or false `closed` flag. Acceptance alone therefore does not establish active status.

`status` distinguishes `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`, `ACTIVE` and `CLOSED`. Access absence is classified as suspended only after a previous activation. `everActivated` permanently records whether activation has occurred. `reason` prioritizes `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, then `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`; it can be empty even when `status` is `CLOSED`.

Initialization through `Clauses Initialized`, monitored `Timeline Access Updated` events, and party-addition requests invoke refresh processing. Initial channel reconciliation uses inert party channels until access is ready. Commits emit `Document Activated` on first activation, `Document Access Suspended` when an active document loses access, and `Document Access Restored` when a previously activated document returns to active from unavailable access. These events carry `revision`.

The exact access-validation and terms-current predicates are inherited and not supplied. Missing state does not itself establish acceptance, access, closure or a configuration default; absence of `/activation` is specifically treated as uninitialized by the dispatch guard.

## Acceptance and roster changes

`approve_<role>` and `updateParty_<role>` operate through party lead channels. Both require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true; an available operation does not itself confer authority.

`approve_<role>` requires `revision` to match `/activation/revision`, a calling channel that identifies a roster party, and valid participant access. When negotiation is enabled, `termsRef` is also required and must match `/activation/terms/ref`; whenever supplied, it must match. A new approval records the party in `approved`, commits readiness, and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. Repeated approval returns successfully without another acceptance event. Success records that party's acceptance and need not activate the document. Activation through this route closes any pending proposal as `SUPERSEDED` and makes negotiation noneditable.

`updateParty_<role>` takes `replacement`, including `lead/channel`, and optional `party`, which defaults to the invoking party. It requires no revision argument, but still requires exact-version review. An existing party can replace only its own data. Adding a new party requires an explicit unused key and `allowNewParties`. Frozen rosters, invalid names, missing lead channels, invalid access for the replacement roster, and contract-name conflicts are rejected. A successful update rebuilds roster contracts, clears all recorded approvals, increments `revision`, and emits `Party Changed`. A directly added party is appended to `required`.

`Party Addition Requested` carries `admissionRef`, `expectedRevision`, `parties` and native Timeline Access `accessDocuments`, keyed by party or `party__representative` transport name. Stale requests and already-recorded admission references are ignored. Processing validates and embeds the supplied public access histories, stores `/activation/accessRequests/<admissionRef>`, and emits `Party Access Update Requested` for existing parties whose timelines need updated reader access. Per-party `ready` values are refreshed while the request revision remains current. These requests neither grant private timeline access nor provide participant consent or owner authority.

The separate `admitApprovedParties` step requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a nonempty `admission/approvers` policy, main-party identity checks, valid resulting access and conflict-free contracts. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster is committed with an incremented revision and `Party Changed` events carrying `admissionRef`. Unlike direct additions, this step does not append admitted keys to `required` or explicitly clear approvals. Negotiation's authority-change rules can still clear them. Receiving an admission request is not confirmation that admission completed.

## Terms and negotiation

`/activation/terms` contains `definition`, a definition identity; `fields`, a map from allowed paths to published scalar values; and `ref`, the identity of those terms together. Initialization excludes documents at `accessPaths`, the activation parameters `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party `readerKeys` from the definition used for this identity. `termsRevision` begins at `1`. Negotiation initializes with `revision: 1`, `editable: true`, and empty `proposal`, `history` and `outcomes` objects.

Configured negotiation creates `proposeChanges_<role>`, `proposeAndActivate_<role>`, `activate_<role>`, `withdrawProposal_<role>`, `rejectProposal_<role>` and `withdrawAcceptance_<role>` for required approvers. These functions require exact-version review and membership of the calling channel in `/activation/required`.

`proposeChanges_<role>` requires a user-selected `proposalId`, matching current `baseTermsRef`, and nonempty `changes`. Each change has required `path` and `replacement`. Paths must be allowed and nonduplicated, replacement values must retain the current value's scalar kind, and the resulting document must match its type. Unchanged terms and reuse of closed proposal identifiers are rejected. Replacing a pending proposal with a different identifier requires `supersedes` to name the current proposal; the old proposal receives outcome `SUPERSEDED`. Recording a proposal does not itself accept or apply it. `proposeAndActivate_<role>` records it and then performs the acceptance step.

`activate_<role>` requires a text `termsRef`. For current terms, `proposalId` must be omitted; the function delegates to approval of the current activation revision. For proposed terms, both the selected proposal identifier and terms reference must match. Stored replacements, their base terms and their resulting identity are revalidated before approval.

Proposed terms are applied only when the inherited amendment-approval step marks that proposal in `negotiation/history`; its precise approval threshold is not supplied. Application replaces the document fields, updates `terms/ref`, increments `termsRevision` and activation `revision`, transfers proposal approvals into `approved`, sets `editable` false, records `APPLIED`, and commits readiness. A successful call can represent an approval still awaiting application.

`withdrawAcceptance_<role>` removes the caller's acceptance of the selected current terms or pending proposal. Current terms require no `proposalId`; proposed terms require matching `proposalId` and `termsRef`. `rejectProposal_<role>` closes the selected pending proposal as `REJECTED`; `withdrawProposal_<role>` closes it as `WITHDRAWN` and additionally requires the caller to be its proposer. Closing records history and clears the pending proposal. A history entry alone does not mean application; `outcomes` distinguishes the result.

New proposals, proposal withdrawal or rejection, and acceptance withdrawal are rejected once `everActivated` is true. Access suspension does not reopen them. A roster or required-approver change updates the terms identity and `termsRevision`, clears a pending proposal with `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation is configured.

## Dispatch guard

This policy always permits its initialization delivery and recognized embedded access-update deliveries, allowing access refresh even while ordinary processing is blocked. Other deliveries require initialized activation state, `accessReady: true`, a fresh successful access check, and a document that is not closed.

After those checks, the policy permits configured external `preActivationOperations`, nonexternal deliveries on `preActivationChannels`, and external deliveries on `preActivationTimerChannels` only when the channel is a Timer Channel. Generated initial-roster approval and update operations, plus configured negotiation operations, are included among pre-activation operations. These exceptions bypass the final business-readiness check, not access or closure checks.

Remaining deliveries use the inherited `businessReady` predicate, whose exact implementation is not supplied, with `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE` as the denial reason. Other installed policies and operation-specific guards still apply. A denied external delivery is consumed and checkpointed, not deferred for replay after activation or restored access.
